newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Boehler sees 1996 net falling 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: Boehler sees 1996 net falling 10 pct.

text.p: Austrian high-grade steelmaker Boehler Uddeholm said on Friday it saw 1996 group net profit falling 10 percent to around one billion schillings ($87 million) due to weaker economic conditions.
In 1995, Boehler posted net profit of 1.11 billion schillings.
Pretax profit is also seen lower at around 1.2 to 1.3 billion schillings after a record 1.35 billion in 1995, chief executive Claus Raidl told investors at a conference in this Alpine resort.
"If you take into consideration that 1995 was a record year for our steel industry and that 1996 was considerably weak, we've been able to achieve very good results", an undaunted Raidl said.
Raidl said 1996 pretax was buoyed by an extraordinary income of 300 million schillings.
Sales are seen falling to 17 billion schillings from 18.3 billion in 1995.

The decline in sales was attributed largely to the loss of turnover from the sale of non-core businesses and an accounting-related deconsolidation of sales in the welding joint venture with Germany's Thyssen group, Raidl said.
Boehler plans to continue its dividend policy.
"Our dividend will be orientated at a dividend yield of three percent and a pay-out ratio in the range between 25 and 30 percent", he said.
Boehler paid a 25 schilling dividend for 1995.
The fiscal year 1996 was marked by a weaker order intake in the field of special steel long products and strip steel, while stable volume and prices prevailed in the welding division, Raidl said.
